title: Claiming Social Security at 70 instead of 67 — who actually wins by 85? 💰

hook.sub: The breakeven math surprises most people.

setup.title: ~$2,000/month at 67 vs ~$2,480/month at 70, lived to age 85.
setup.foot: Waiting increases the monthly check by roughly 8% per year delayed.

tension.ask: Who comes out ahead by age 85?

twist.l2: At 85, the later claim wins here.
twist.l3: Your health and longevity matter more than the rule of thumb.

vo.hook: Why does the "right" age to claim Social Security depend so heavily on how long you actually live?
vo.setup: Claiming at 67 pays about $2,000 a month. Waiting until 70 pays about $2,480 a month, roughly eight percent more per year delayed.
vo.tension: Starting sooner means more total checks. Starting later means bigger checks. Who actually comes out ahead by age 85?
vo.reveal: Total lifetime benefit to age 85: claiming at 67 totals about $432k. Claiming at 70 totals about $446k.
vo.twist: There's no universal right answer — at age 85, the later claim wins, but your own health and longevity matter more than any rule of thumb. Run your own scenario on wealthdelay dot com, link below.

disclaimer: Hypothetical based on stated benefit amounts and an approximate 8%/year delayed-retirement credit; actual benefits depend on your work history and SSA rules. Not financial advice.
